key_insight: PsychFound is a psychiatry-specialized LLM trained on expert knowledge and clinical records that achieves clinical-grade performance and measurably improves diagnostic and treatment decisions when embedded in clinician workflows.
problem_solved: General-purpose LLMs lack the domain-specific knowledge, reliability, and workflow integration needed for safe, actionable psychiatric clinical decision support; this work closes that gap by adapting a model specifically for psychiatric practice and validating it in clinical settings.
method: Domain adaptation of a large language model using curated psychiatry textbooks, guidelines, and expert-annotated knowledge to inject specialist priors.
Fine-tuning on de-identified psychiatric clinical records and case notes to align the model with real-world clinical language and workflows.
Rigorous clinical evaluation (benchmarking against standards and clinician review) and deployment tests to measure impact on diagnostic and treatment decisions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows that targeted domain adaptation plus clinically sourced data can produce LLMs with actionable, clinical-grade behavior—and underscores the importance of domain-specific evaluation, safety checks, and workflow integration when deploying models in healthcare.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: base LLM → domain adaptation (expert knowledge) → fine-tuning (clinical records) → deployed Clinician+Model loop
Performance bar chart: PsychFound vs. general LLMs on diagnostic accuracy, treatment recommendation quality, and safety metrics
Clinical workflow schematic: how model outputs integrate into clinician decision points (triage, diagnosis, treatment planning)
Case vignette panel: before/after example showing model’s diagnostic suggestions and clinician acceptance/changes
paper_title: A domain-adapted large language model to support clinicians in psychiatric clinical practice
paper_authors: Ruoxi Wang, Shuyu Liu, Ling Zhang, Xuequan Zhu, Zhi Yang
